title: 30-minute Beginner Belly Dance Class with Portia!

observation_window.sampling: provider default; not continuous motion capture

extraction.teacher_style: Portia maintains a warm and encouraging tone throughout the class, frequently checking in with students while breaking down movements step-by-step. She combines verbal instructions with constant physical demonstration, emphasizing posture, breathing, and body awareness.

lesson_structure.note: Teacher introduces the beginner belly dance class and playlist.
Teacher guides a full-body warmup starting with posture and breathing.
Spine roll and standing cat-and-cow stretches.
Side view demonstration of pelvic rocking and lower abs engagement.
Foot massage, chest lifts, and heel weight placement practice.

safety: Keep knees soft and avoid locking them

steps_taught.name: Standing Cat and Cow
steps_taught.description: Spine roll down and up with bent knees.

steps_taught.name: Plié with Pelvic Rock
steps_taught.description: Wide stance squat with gentle lower abdominal tucks.

what_works: Clear visual demonstrations from multiple angles
Frequent reminders on breathing and posture
what_hinders: Continuous talking can sometimes overlap with counting

quotes.text: Today, nonstop movement, we're going to start with basics.
Now I do a lot of talking, but I want you to breathe.
I know it's hard. If you have to go smaller with the plié, that's okay.
Let's go, let's go, up, go big.

evidence_segments.observation: Teacher demonstrates wide stance setup with softened knees and diagonal foot placement.
evidence_segments.cannot_infer: exact muscle tension in the lower back

evidence_segments.observation: Teacher performs a spinal roll down with hands on thighs, then rolls back up.
evidence_segments.cannot_infer: degree of spinal articulation in individual students

evidence_segments.observation: Teacher shifts to a side profile to demonstrate pelvic rocking and abdominal tucks.

extraction.distinctive_method: Integrating continuous breath work prompts ("inhale through the nose, exhale and sit down") directly into the physical warmup movements.
